title: Deepest lakes
measure: Maximum depth in metres, from the surface to the deepest known point. Includes the Caspian Sea, which geographers usually class as a lake, and Lake Vostok, which lies under the Antarctic ice. Ranked by maximum depth, not average depth.

entries.name: Baikal
entries.note: Also the largest freshwater lake by volume.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Tanganyika
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Caspian Sea
entries.note: Called a sea, but generally classed by geographers and limnologists as a huge inland salt lake.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Vostok
entries.location: Under the East Antarctic Ice Sheet
entries.note: A lake sealed under about 4 km of ice. Its depth, from 510 m to about 900 m across the lake, comes from radar and seismic surveys, not direct measurement.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: O'Higgins / San Martín
entries.note: The deepest lake in the Americas.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Argentino
entries.note: Left out of many older top 10 lists.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Malawi
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Great Slave
entries.note: The deepest lake in North America.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of lakes by depth (March 2026)

entries.name: Crater Lake
entries.note: Lake Matano in Indonesia (590 m) is just 4 m behind.
